confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for Naha prices. The price sources were crowdsourced or aggregated cost-of-living sites (Expatistan, Numbeo-derived pages, mylifeelsewhere, livingcost-style pages) plus a few listing sites. They disagree and some are dated. Typical Naha figures were roughly: inexpensive meal 800 to 1,600 yen, cappuccino 430 to 670 yen, and draft beer a few hundred yen at casual izakaya. I weighed these toward tourist-area bar and restaurant prices, so beer is set above the lowest crowdsourced figures. I found no Naha cocktail price and no per-glass wine price. Cocktail is set at about twice the beer price and wine glass at about 1.6 times the beer price, based on typical Japanese izakaya and bar price relationships. The mid-range meal for two is the least certain food anchor: sources ranged from about $25 to $30 (crowdsourced) up to a higher figure for a typical sit-down dinner in tourist areas. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July (peak season), not from live listings or searches. Accommodation is the least certain group. The FX rate comes from a web search result summarising the RBA exchange-rates page and homepage, not from a direct page read by me.
comparable_city_reasoning: Regional Japanese resort city, a little cheaper than Tokyo for food and coffee but with a strong domestic tourism premium on accommodation in summer. Informal sources put Naha restaurants about 7% above the Japan average.
